text.p: Swiss food and hotel group Moevenpick AG said it expected a return to sales growth this year after two years of decline and continued steady growth in profits.
Moevenpick also said the expected improvements in sales and the potential for profit gains came despite a difficult economic climate.
"We believe that the sales shrinkage of 1996 has come to a halt," Moevenpick said in its annual report.
"As of the new business year (1997), we once again expect sales to grow," it added.
In its annual report to shareholders, Moevenpick chief executive Ulrich Geissmann said that the economic situation remained difficult.

"The outlook for the near year remains problematic from an economic standpoint. But for Moevenpick it (the outlook) is positive in spite of that, because we have become capable of making continual progress in this environment, and because several dozen projects for the future are already under contract," it said.
Moevenpick also said there would be a shift from sales by its consolidated activities to revenue from businesses under management contracts and franchises. It did not elaborate.
Moevenpick said the sales growth brought more potential for rising profits.
"We do not expect any spectacular improvements, because we have to count on a continued difficult consumer climate in both main markets," it said, referring to Switzerland and Germany.
"But expansion abroad...should have a gradual effect of creating continued, positive profit contributions," it added.

The company already announced in March that 1996 group net profit rose to 22.4 million Swiss francs ($15.2 million) from 15.2 million in 1995. Moevenpick reported 1996 sales of 1.112 billion Swiss francs, down 0.3 percent from 1.116 billion in 1995.
It also planned to raise its dividend on 1996 results to 14 percent per nominal share or certificate, equaling seven francs per bearer share.
This was increased from 12 percent, or six francs per bearer.
The company announced in March that 1996 group net profit rose to 22.4 million Swiss francs from 15.2 million in 1995.

Moevenpick total sales declined from 1.16 billion Swiss francs in 1994 to 1.12 billion francs last year as the group divested and trimmed some businesses and under the impact of weak economies with poor consumer demand in Switzerland and Germany.
